cards.back: Control in which a response reduces the deviation that elicited it.
A condition where state variables are constant in time because net rates of change are zero; flows may continue.
The membrane voltage at which the net current carried by a particular ion is zero.
A measure of how readily charge flows; in I = g(V − E), it scales current for a given driving force.
Blood flow through a tissue's microvasculature.
A spatial imbalance between air reaching alveoli and blood reaching their capillaries.
The virtual volume of plasma cleared of a substance per unit time, calculated from urine and plasma concentrations.
A response that helps maintain a regulated variable while potentially changing system load or reserve.
C = 1.34 × Hb × S + 0.003 × P_O₂ (mL/dL); hemoglobin and saturation dominate.
V̇O₂ = Q̇ (C_a − C_v); any three determine the fourth.
DO₂ = Q̇ × C_a; extraction = V̇O₂/DO₂, about 0.25 at rest for the whole body.
Lower content is offset by higher cardiac output and higher extraction, which lowers venous saturation.
C = U × V̇ / P: plasma volume completely cleared per unit time.
Inulin clearance ≈ GFR; PAH clearance ≈ renal plasma flow; filtration fraction = GFR/RPF ≈ 0.2.
Excretion = filtered load − T_m once load exceeds T_m; real kidneys show splay.
Below GFR: net reabsorption; above GFR: net secretion; use the unbound plasma concentration.
J_v = K_f[(P_c − P_i) − σ(π_c − π_i)]; positive means filtration out.
Net pressure falls with P_c; many tissues filter along most of the length, with lymph returning fluid.
Higher P_c, lower π_c, leaky walls (lower σ, higher K_f) or blocked lymph.
Rising P_i and falling π_i oppose further filtration until exhausted.
C_ss = P/CL; τ = V/CL; 63% at one τ and 90% at τ ln 10; halving clearance doubles both C_ss and τ.
About 20 kJ per liter of O₂; heat storage S = M − W − H_loss; ΔT rate = S/(mass × 3.5 kJ/(kg·°C)).
Closed-loop deviation e = d/(1 + G); G = (open-loop deviation / closed-loop deviation) − 1; proportional control leaves a residual error.
A changed set point is defended by working effectors; failure shows effectors overwhelmed or absent.
E = (RT/zF) ln([out]/[in]); about 61.5 mV × log₁₀(ratio)/z at 37 °C.
V = Σ g E / Σ g (conductance form) or the GHK equation (permeability form); it sits between E_K and E_Na, closest to the ion with the largest conductance.
E_K shifts about 61.5 mV per tenfold change; the resting potential shifts less because sodium permeability pulls it toward E_Na.
Depolarization moves a cell toward threshold, but sustained depolarization inactivates sodium channels, so the net effect depends on size and duration.
MAP − CVP = CO × TPR; Q = ΔP/R for any vessel or bed; CO = HR × SV.
1/R_total = Σ 1/R_i; the total is lower than any branch; opening a bed lowers TPR and diverts flow.
R = 8μL/(πr⁴): halving the radius multiplies resistance by 16; the law is a scaling guide for rigid laminar flow.
PP ≈ SV/C; stiffer arteries widen pulse pressure at the same mean pressure; MAP ≈ DBP + PP/3.
V̇_A = (V_T − V_D) × f; shallow fast breathing lowers it at the same minute ventilation.
P_ACO₂ ≈ 0.863 × V̇_CO₂/V̇_A: halving alveolar ventilation doubles alveolar CO₂.
P_AO₂ = F_IO₂ (P_B − P_H₂O) − P_aCO₂/R; hypoventilation lowers O₂ and raises CO₂ with a normal A–a gradient.
1/C_total = 1/C_lung + 1/C_wall; shunt fraction = (C_c − C_a)/(C_c − C_v), poorly corrected by extra oxygen.
F₀ = σ₀ × PCSA; about 25 N/cm² in the synthetic examples; force scales with area, not length.
Force depends on filament overlap: a plateau near 2.2 μm and a linear descent to zero near 3.6 μm.
(F + a)(v + b) = (F₀ + a) b; v = b (F₀ − F)/(F + a); v_max = bF₀/a.
P = F v is zero at F = 0 and v = 0 and peaks at F* = F₀[√((a/F₀)(a/F₀ + 1)) − a/F₀], about 0.31 F₀ for a/F₀ = 0.25.
Hemostasis (minutes), inflammation (hours–days), proliferation (days–weeks), remodeling (weeks–months); phases overlap.
Repair restores continuity, often with a scar; regeneration restores original structure and function and needs structure, function, lineage and controls as evidence.
Gap width W closes at 2v: t_c = W/(2v); fraction closed = 2vt/W; speed per edge = closed width/2/time.
Separate migration from proliferation, image the same fields, use independent replicates, fit a rate from several time points, and state what a flat culture leaves out.
Average open area at each time across independent experiments; report the number of experiments.
Rate = percentage points of area closed / hours, preferably from a fit across several time points.
If closure is nearly unchanged when division is blocked, migration accounts for most of it over that time.
A flat layer of one cell type shows effects on migration and division in culture, not on healing in tissue.
A regulated value can be held by different combinations of output and resistance; the cost appears in organ flow, extraction and effort.
Reserve = maximum capacity − current use; compensation uses reserve, so a normal resting value can coexist with little reserve.
Apply a graded challenge: reserve shows as how far the controlled value is held when demand rises.
Choose a measurement that could contradict it: challenge response, direct organ flow, venous oxygen or hormone levels, not another resting reading.
Volume is on the horizontal axis and pressure on the vertical axis; filling, isovolumic contraction, ejection and isovolumic relaxation trace one beat.
SV = EDV − ESV; the horizontal width of a pressure-volume loop is volume ejected per beat.
The magnitude of ∮P dV estimates external stroke work per beat; 1 mmHg·mL = 1.33322×10⁻⁴ J.
Work depends on both pressure and loop width; a rectangular mean-pressure estimate is conditional and is not a clinical prediction.
τ_m = R_m C_m does not depend on cell size; a current step reaches 63% of its final voltage after one τ_m.
A compact cell's input resistance is R_m divided by its surface area, so small cells respond to small currents.
λ = √(r_m/r_i) = √(R_m a/(2R_i)); a steady voltage falls to 37% at one λ, and λ grows only as √a.
Unmyelinated velocity scales roughly with √a; myelin raises R_m and lowers C_m, giving saltatory conduction roughly proportional to diameter.

cards.front: Membrane equation for a space-clamped patch
cards.back: C_m dV/dt = −(I_Na + I_K + I_L) + I_stim, with I_x = g_x (V − E_x); in a voltage clamp dV/dt = 0, so the injected current equals the ionic current.
dx/dt = α(1 − x) − βx, so x relaxes to x∞ = α/(α + β) with time constant τ = 1/(α + β).
g_K = ḡ_K n⁴ and g_Na = ḡ_Na m³h; m is fast, while h (inactivation) and n are several times slower.
Absolute: no stimulus triggers a spike while too few sodium channels have recovered (low h). Relative: a stronger stimulus can, while h recovers and n is still raised.

cards.front: Why does a reference clearance require more than a concentration ratio?
cards.back: Multiplying U/P by urine flow supplies volume per time; filtration-only handling is then needed to interpret that clearance as GFR.

cards.front: Why compare filtered and excreted mass rates rather than plasma and urine concentrations directly?
cards.back: Water flow changes concentration. Rates on the same mg/min basis close the balance and expose net transport.

cards.front: Can clearance above GFR identify a transporter or quantify both opposing fluxes?
cards.back: No. In the declared freely filtered, nonmetabolized model it shows net secretion, while multiple gross-flux combinations can produce that same net rate.

cards.front: Why use max(filtered load − Tm, 0) rather than subtracting Tm unconditionally?
cards.back: The ideal model cannot excrete a negative mass rate below the saturation threshold; the expression assumes complete reabsorption below Tm.

cards.front: What is the narrowest conclusion of this renal ledger?
cards.back: Given the stipulated reference and transport assumptions, it identifies model mass rates and net handling. It supplies no clinical estimate, test or treatment decision.
Multiply the remaining fractions in sequence, retaining a filtered-input/output/reabsorbed amount ledger. Adding removal fractions double counts the same solute.

cards.front: Why solve water and solute balances separately?
cards.back: Their transport controls and units differ. Concentration emerges from both amount output and volume output, rather than providing a substitute for either ledger.

cards.front: Does dilute urine necessarily mean less solute excretion?
cards.back: No. Compare concentration times urine flow; changes in the denominator can dilute the same solute output.

cards.front: What does a mechanistic nephron explanation add to a clearance ratio?
cards.back: It distinguishes segment transport, water permeability, driving gradients and hormonal control; a single output ratio cannot identify all those mechanisms.

cards.front: Why can negative feedback leave a nonzero steady error?
cards.back: Finite gain reduces a sustained disturbance by 1+gk; it does not necessarily eliminate the error in this proportional two-state model.

cards.front: What does a stable complex eigenpair establish?
cards.back: Decaying oscillatory homogeneous modes for the specified linear system; peaks, settling criteria and other nonlinear/delayed models need additional analysis.

cards.front: How do you verify a bounded-controller equilibrium?
cards.back: Solve the balance on the proposed branch, then check that the unbounded target actually belongs to that branch.

cards.front: Why keep bias, gain and saturation perturbations separate?
cards.back: They alter different equations or branches. Similar observed regulated values can conceal different mechanisms and reserve limits.

cards.front: Which quantity must be mixed in parallel blood streams?
cards.back: Add oxygen amount rates Q C, then divide by total blood flow; pressure is not itself a conserved oxygen amount.

cards.front: When can an inverse content curve be used after mixing?
cards.back: Only within the declared shared binding conditions and admissible content domain. A real mixed-stream pressure may need additional chemistry and dissolved-oxygen terms.

cards.front: How are oxygen delivery and tissue uptake distinguished?
cards.back: Delivery is Q Ca; uptake is Q(Ca−Cv) under a steady conserved blood-flow boundary. Their difference is returning venous oxygen.

cards.front: Why is a fitted equivalent bypass fraction not a unique diagnosis of mechanism?
cards.back: Several mechanisms can produce the same mixed content; discriminate them with additional controlled measurements and an explicit model boundary.

cards.front: What makes a membrane simulation independently checkable?
cards.back: A unit ledger, initial derivative, analytic passive limit, gate invariance and convergence checks, with the stimulus/clamp boundary stated explicitly.

cards.front: Does a fourth-power conductance always start with zero slope?
cards.back: No. Its right-hand slope is 4 gbar n0³ ndot(0+), nonzero for a nonzero gate with a nonzero initial derivative.

cards.front: What belongs in a gas-exchange evidence report?
cards.back: Binding assumptions, flow/content amount balances, delivery versus uptake, controlled perturbations and an explicit account of which mechanisms remain unidentifiable.

cards.front: Can mixed oxygen content improve while total delivery declines?
cards.back: Yes. Selectively reducing a low-content stream can raise the mixture content while reducing total flow and its oxygen amount rate.

cards.front: Which consistency checks should a serial nephron solver retain?
cards.back: Nonnegative delivered amounts, removal/output conservation, filtered input, unit conversions, and separate water/solute ledgers before forming concentration or clearance.
Otherwise one can carry changed parameters into a later comparison and attribute a coupled result to the wrong single control.

cards.front: What should be verified before interpreting a simulated transient?
cards.back: Initial conditions and derivatives, equilibrium residuals, linear modes, units/scales and integration refinement; plots alone can hide sign or boundary errors.

cards.front: How can a normal-looking regulated quantity hide impaired reserve?
cards.back: An observed value is only one output. Disturbance response, control effort, saturation, bias and model assumptions determine what capacity can be inferred.
pH = 6.1 + log₁₀([HCO₃⁻]/(0.03 × P_CO₂)), with bicarbonate in mmol/L and P_CO₂ in mmHg. pH depends on the ratio, so doubling both terms leaves it unchanged and doubling P_CO₂ alone lowers it by 0.30.
pH depends only on the ratio of bicarbonate to dissolved CO₂. A rise in P_CO₂ and a fall in bicarbonate can give the same ratio, so a second measurement is needed to name the term that moved.

Compensation moves the other term in the same direction, but a proportional controller needs a remaining error to act. The closed-loop deviation is d/(1 + G), so the compensation removes G/(1 + G) of the disturbance and never all of it.

cards.front: A small fraction of a large flow
cards.back: Filtered bicarbonate is about 180 L/day × 24 mmol/L = 4320 mmol/day. A 1% reabsorption shortfall is 43 mmol/day, comparable to the model's 70 mmol/day acid load, so the kidney must be nearly exact.
AG = Na⁺ − Cl⁻ − HCO₃⁻ equals unmeasured anions minus unmeasured cations by electroneutrality. It is bookkeeping: it is not a pH measurement and says nothing about P_CO₂.

A valve is open when upstream pressure exceeds downstream pressure. Both valves are closed in isovolumic contraction and isovolumic relaxation, so pressure alone cannot separate those phases; the direction of change does.

cards.front: Why output can peak and then fall
cards.back: Diastole shortens by a larger fraction than systole as rate rises, so stroke volume falls with filling time. CO = HR × SV rises until the fall in SV outweighs the rise in rate; in the stipulated model the peak is near 126 per minute.

t = d/v. A 5 mm segment at 0.05 m/s contributes 0.10 s of a 0.16 s total because the velocity is far lower than in atrial or Purkinje tissue, letting atrial contraction finish before the ventricle contracts.

II = I + III. The limb leads are differences of the same three potentials (I = LA − RA, II = LL − RA, III = LL − LA), so the second lead is the sum of the other two. Each lead records p cos(θ − its axis angle).
